# sshboard

> A desktop SSH client where a human and an AI agent hold **the same one
> connection**. The agent works through an MCP server built into the app, and
> everything it does lands on a screen the human is sitting in front of. Tauri 2
> + SvelteKit shell, Rust core, MIT-licensed, self-hosted only — there is no
> service to sign up for.

This file exists because the README is long and the part you probably need —
how to connect, and what you are and are not allowed to do — is spread across
it. If you were asked to "connect sshboard", read the two sections below and
stop.

**Three facts worth having before you read anything else.**

**There is no `run_command(cmd)` tool.** Not a filtered one, not a clever one.
An agent cannot hand an arbitrary string to a shell. Read-only commands come
from an allow-list a human wrote in `readonly.toml`, which **starts empty** —
out of the box you cannot run a single command.

**Writes are fenced to directories a human listed**, per connection, and that
list also starts empty. Upload and mkdir only: no delete, rename, move, chmod,
service restart or package install. There is **no download-to-my-machine
tool** — the fence does not protect the human's laptop, so no door is opened
onto it.

**Anything that changes state needs a human press.** The first attempt is
always refused so the screen can show exactly what would run. Approvals expire
in five minutes and cover one run.

## Connect sshboard as an MCP server

The app must be running. This form starts sshboard as a relay with no window,
so the token is never written to disk — not into `~/.claude.json`, not into
shell history:

```sh
# macOS
claude mcp add sshboard -- /Applications/sshboard.app/Contents/MacOS/sshboard --mcp-stdio-proxy

# Windows
claude mcp add sshboard -- "%LOCALAPPDATA%\sshboard\sshboard.exe" --mcp-stdio-proxy
```

The port is fixed at `22022` and the token is reused, so this is a one-time
step; restarting the app does not make you register again. If the port is
taken it says so on screen rather than quietly moving.

## Call `about_sshboard` first

That tool exists so you can find out what this is, what you may and may not do,
and what changed in each version, without a human pasting a briefing. It
touches no remote server and puts nothing on the human's screen.

## What you can do

36 tools over MCP, in seven groups: connecting and choosing where operations
go; looking at the server (listing, stat, reading files, search, disk usage,
processes, listening ports, service status, runtime versions); writing inside
the fence; running commands from the human's allow-lists; the shared terminal;
the human's screen; and sshboard itself.

The terminal is **shared**. While you hold it the human's input is locked out
and a Stop button is showing on their screen — they can take it back at any
time, and every keystroke you send is visible to them as you send it.

## Sibling projects

- **dbboard** — the same idea for databases: a desktop client plus an MCP
  server, read-only unless a human opts a connection in.
  https://meta-taro.github.io/dbboard/
- **warifu** — people and agents in one conversation, peer to peer, with no
  central account. https://meta-taro.github.io/warifu/
